title: Bali Luxury Honeymoon: 7 Days in Nusa Dua & Ubud
meta_title: Bali Honeymoon Package 7 Days | Nusa Dua & Ubud | Blue Diamond Voyage
meta_description: 7-day Bali honeymoon itinerary: 6 nights in a honeymoon suite at Nusa Dua, Lempuyang Gates of Heaven, Tanah Lot sunset, scuba diving and a candlelight dinner in Ubud.
price_note: Price on request. Tailored to your dates, flights and hotel choice.
best_time: April to October (dry season). Avoid Nyepi, Bali's Day of Silence in March, when the airport and roads close for 24 hours.
hero_alt: Bali temple and rice terraces at sunrise
intro: A slow, romantic week that pairs a beachfront honeymoon suite in Nusa Dua with Bali's most photogenic temples, a sunset at Tanah Lot, your first scuba dive and a private candlelight dinner in an Ubud garden. Every transfer is private, and every day is paced around Bali's traffic and temple timings so you spend your time together, not in a car.
highlights: 6 nights in a Honeymoon Suite at The Crystal Luxury Bay Resort, Nusa Dua (half board)
Private East Bali photo tour: Lempuyang 'Gates of Heaven', Tirta Gangga Water Palace, Goa Raja Waterfall and Tegalalang Rice Terraces
Tanah Lot sea temple at sunset
Discover Scuba Dive for beginners with an English-speaking instructor
Private candlelight dinner in a garden in Ubud
Private SUV airport transfers and a dedicated 24x7 Blue Diamond Voyage contact

days.title: Arrive in Bali, check in to your honeymoon suite
days.body: Land at Bali Ngurah Rai International Airport (DPS). Your private driver meets you at arrivals (up to 60 minutes' wait included) for the 25 to 35 minute drive to Nusa Dua. Check in to your Honeymoon Suite at The Crystal Luxury Bay Resort and spend the afternoon on Nusa Dua's calm, reef-protected beach. Dinner at the resort (half board).
days.tip: Indonesia offers visa on arrival or e-VOA for Indian passport holders. Apply for the e-VOA online before you fly to skip the airport queue, and keep your return ticket and hotel booking handy.

days.title: East Bali photo tour: Gates of Heaven & rice terraces
days.body: A private full-day tour with a professional guide. Lempuyang is about 2.5 to 3 hours' drive from Nusa Dua, so we start early to beat the queue for the famous 'Gates of Heaven' photo framing Mount Agung. Continue to Tirta Gangga, the former royal water palace with its stepping stones and koi ponds, then the cave waterfall at Goa Raja, and finish at the Tegalalang Rice Terraces on the way back via Ubud.
days.tip: Temples require covered shoulders and knees. A sarong is lent at Lempuyang for a small donation. Women who are menstruating are traditionally asked not to enter temple grounds; please respect this. Expect a 1 to 2 hour wait for the Gates of Heaven photo on busy days.

days.title: Morning at leisure, Tanah Lot at sunset
days.body: Sleep in, enjoy a couples' spa treatment or the resort pools. Leave around 15:00 for Tanah Lot, about 1 hour 15 minutes away, to explore the 16th-century sea temple perched on a rock in the Indian Ocean and watch the sunset from the cliff-top cafés. Back at the resort by around 20:30.
days.tip: Only Hindu worshippers may climb onto the temple rock itself. At low tide you can walk to its base and receive holy spring water and a blessing. Check tide timings with us.

days.title: Discover Scuba Dive
days.body: No experience needed. After a short theory lesson and equipment briefing, dive with an English-speaking instructor at all times to see coral reefs, sea turtles and tropical fish. Allow 5 to 6 hours including the boat. We pick the dive site around your dates and sea conditions: Nusa Dua, Nusa Penida or Amed for a day trip, or Lombok and the Gili Islands if you add a night there.
days.tip: Do not fly within 18 hours of diving, which is why we schedule the dive early in your trip. Divers must be in good health. Let us know about any medical conditions in advance.

days.title: Ubud culture & candlelight dinner
days.body: Drive about 1 hour 15 minutes to Ubud, Bali's cultural heart. Walk through the Sacred Monkey Forest, browse the Ubud Art Market and see Ubud Palace. In the evening (from 18:00), enjoy a private 2-hour candlelight dinner for two in a lush Ubud garden. Private transfer back to Nusa Dua.
days.tip: Keep sunglasses, earrings and snacks out of sight in the Monkey Forest. The macaques are quick. Ubud is the best place for an evening Legong or Kecak dance performance.

days.title: Free day: beach, spa or Uluwatu
days.body: A day just for the two of you. Relax at the resort, try a Balinese massage, or (optional) visit Uluwatu Temple, 30 minutes away, for the cliff-top Kecak fire dance at sunset, followed by a seafood dinner on Jimbaran Bay.
days.tip: Uluwatu's monkeys also snatch belongings. The Kecak dance starts around 18:00. We pre-book seats to avoid the ticket queue.

days.title: Departure
days.body: Breakfast and check-out. Your private driver transfers you to the airport about 3 hours before your flight. Allow extra time on Friday and weekend evenings, when traffic on the Bali Mandara toll road and bypass is heaviest.

faqs.q: When is the best time for a honeymoon in Bali?
faqs.a: April to October is the dry season with sunny days and calm seas, ideal for beaches, temples and diving. November to March is the wet season. It's greener and quieter, with short tropical showers, usually in the afternoon.

faqs.q: Is Nusa Dua or Ubud better for a honeymoon?
faqs.a: Nusa Dua offers calm beaches and luxury resorts, while Ubud offers jungle villas, rice terraces and culture. This itinerary bases you in Nusa Dua and takes you to Ubud for a day and a romantic dinner. We can also split your stay, for example 3 nights in Ubud and 3 in Nusa Dua.

faqs.q: Do Indian citizens need a visa for Bali?
faqs.a: Indian passport holders can get a visa on arrival or apply online for an e-VOA before travel. Your passport needs at least 6 months' validity. We guide you through the process and current fees when you book.
Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change hotels, add Nusa Penida, the Gili Islands or a private villa with a pool, and plan flights from your city.

faqs.q: Is vegetarian or Jain food available in Bali?
faqs.a: Yes. Bali has many vegetarian and Indian restaurants, especially in Ubud, Seminyak and Nusa Dua. Tell us your dietary needs and we will inform the resort and choose restaurants for you.
